items.entity: L-shaped design domain (size and position of the removed corner, arm widths)
items.description: Sec. 4 'Example designs' and the Fig. 4 caption only say 'classic L-shaped bracket'. The out-of-distribution problems come from 28 parameterized classes 'with the parameters drawn at random from a uniform distribution' (Sec. 3.1 'Dataset'; Sec. 3.2 'Benchmarking problem sets'), and the values drawn for this example are never reported. The orientation (cutout at top-right, vertical arm on the left, horizontal arm at the bottom) can only be inferred from 'classic' plus 'clamped top edge / load at right edge'. The actual geometry is visible only in Fig. 4.
readings: Square L x L bounding box with a top-right square cutout of side 0.6L (both arms 0.4L wide; classic L-bracket)
Top-right square cutout of side 0.5L (arms 0.5L wide)
Top-right square cutout of side 0.7L (arms 0.3L wide)
Top-right square cutout of side 0.8L (arms 0.2L wide)

items.entity: Removed corner of the L on the structured grid
items.description: The text never says how the L-shape is built for the compliance runs. The training set used a 'square mask to restrict part of the design domain from applying material' (Sec. 3.1 'Dataset'), and the decoder always outputs a full 64x64 field, which suggests a masked corner on a square grid. The text does not say how masked elements are handled in the FE model or in the cone filter (Sec. 3.1; 'Topology optimization set-up').
readings: Cutout elements kept as passive void (rho=0, E=Emin=1e-9); standard cone filter over all elements; cutout reset to 0 after filtering
Passive void with a mask-aware cone filter (weights normalized over designable elements only)
Cutout elements deleted from the FE mesh (true L-shaped mesh)

items.entity: Clamped support on the top edge
items.description: The Fig. 4 caption says 'clamped support along the top edge'. When an L-shape sits inside a square grid, this could mean only the top edge of the vertical arm, or the whole top edge of the bounding box, including nodes that border the void cutout. Whether the re-entrant-corner node is included is also unstated.
readings: Both DOFs fixed at all nodes on the top edge of the vertical arm only, x from 0 to a*L (a = arm-width fraction)
Both DOFs fixed at all nodes along the full top edge of the square grid, x from 0 to L (nodes above the cutout touch only void elements)

items.entity: Downward point load on the right edge
items.description: The Fig. 4 caption says only 'a downward point load applied at the right edge'. The right edge here is the tip of the horizontal arm, running from (1-a)L to L below the top edge, where a is the arm-width fraction. The text does not give which node on that edge is loaded; out-of-distribution parameters were drawn at random (Sec. 3.1), so it is visible only in the figure.
readings: Upper corner of the arm tip: x = L, y = (1-a)L below the top (e.g. 0.6L for a = 0.4)
Mid-height of the arm tip: x = L, y = (1-a/2)L below the top (e.g. 0.8L for a = 0.4)
Bottom-right corner: x = L, y = L

items.description: No force magnitude is given for the Fig. 4 problem or any compliance benchmark (Sec. 3.1, Sec. 3.2, Fig. 4 caption). Results are reported only as errors relative to MMA.
readings: F = 1 (unit load, consistent with the E0 = 1 normalization)
Another constant magnitude, e.g. F = 10

items.entity: Prescribed volume fraction V0 for the L-bracket
items.description: Not reported for this example. Training volume fractions were drawn from U[0.12, 0.5] (Sec. 3.1 'Dataset'). The out-of-distribution set instead uses the Hoyer et al. classes with randomly drawn parameters, and the value drawn here is not given in the text or caption.

items.entity: Reference area for the volume fraction
items.description: Eq. (2) requires the integral of rho over 'the design domain Omega' to equal V0. For the L-bracket it does not say whether Omega is the L-shaped designable region or the full square grid with the cutout counted as void.
readings: V0 as a fraction of the L-shaped designable area only
V0 as a fraction of the full square grid (cutout counted as zero density)

items.description: Sec. 3.1 'Dataset' and 'Topology optimization set-up' give E0 = 1.0, Emin = 1e-9 and nu = 0.3 'following the approach of the 88-line code'. They never give the SIMP penalty p, which is an input to that code, or any continuation scheme.
readings: p = 3 (fixed)
p raised by continuation, e.g. 1 -> 3
p = 4 (fixed)

items.entity: FE discretization of the L-bracket domain
items.description: The text says only that designs, and the LBAE/VAE inputs and outputs, are 64x64 grayscale images 'with pixel values representing the volume fraction', and that the filter radius is '2 pixels' (Sec. 3.1 'Architecture', 'Dataset'). The FE mesh, element size and bounding-box aspect ratio are never stated for this problem. Only the fracture example states an explicit FE grid (64x128, with resizing).
readings: 64 x 64 unit square Q4 elements, one element per image pixel (square bounding box)
Finer FE mesh (e.g. 128 x 128) with designs resampled to 64 x 64 images (filter radius scaled to match)

items.description: Sec. 3.1 'Dataset' says MMA was run 'with the default hyperparameter settings' 'for 200 iterations'. It does not say which MMA implementation was used, so move limits and asymptote defaults are unknown. The starting design is stated only for the fracture example (uniform at the volume fraction). It is also unclear whether the volume constraint was an explicit MMA constraint or the Eq. (2) sigmoid/bisection mapping.
readings: Uniform start rho = V0; Svanberg MMA defaults (move limit 0.5); explicit volume constraint; 200 iterations
Uniform start rho = V0; MMA with move limit 0.2; explicit volume constraint; 200 iterations
Uniform start; NLopt MMA defaults (no explicit move limit); explicit volume constraint; 200 iterations
MMA on unconstrained logits mapped through the Eq. (2) volume-preserving sigmoid; 200 iterations

items.entity: Thresholding used for the binary designs and errors shown in Fig. 4
items.description: Sec. 3.2 'Performance metrics' says binary designs use 'the simplest strategy from [66]' as a post-processing step, without describing it. Only the thermal example (Sec. 4) says thresholding rounds to 0/1 'while preserving the volume fraction'.
readings: Volume-preserving: set the V0*N highest-density elements to 1 and the rest to 0
Fixed cut-off: rho >= 0.5 -> 1, otherwise 0

locator: Sec. 4 'Example designs', Fig. 4 (the first problem instance shown with a design)
